domain_symbols.shape_data: finite geometric and topological data structures

rules.name: Convex hull algorithmic seed
rules.input_form: finite point set
preconditions: A finite point set is fixed in an ambient affine or Euclidean space
rules.operation: Form the minimal convex set containing all sample points.
examples: Point-cloud boundary structure is often reduced first to its convex hull before finer geometric analysis
counterexamples: Arbitrary polygons passing through sample points are not automatically convex hulls

rules.name: Voronoi-Delaunay duality seed
rules.input_form: finite Euclidean site configuration
preconditions: A finite set of sites is fixed in a standard Euclidean setting
rules.operation: Relate nearest-site Voronoi cells to the dual Delaunay triangulation.
examples: Nearest-site partition data and triangulation connectivity encode the same geometric configuration from dual viewpoints
counterexamples: An arbitrary triangulation of sample points is not automatically the Delaunay dual of the Voronoi diagram

rules.name: Sweep-order seed
rules.input_form: geometric event family with an ordered traversal parameter
preconditions: A total or partial event order is fixed
rules.operation: Reduce geometric reasoning to event ordering with active state updates.
examples: Intersection and arrangement computations can be organized by event ordering instead of naive pairwise search
counterexamples: Ignoring event-order updates breaks the correctness of sweep-based reasoning

rules.name: Simplicial complex data seed
rules.input_form: finite simplex and face-incidence data
preconditions: Face-closure and incidence compatibility are fixed
rules.operation: Encode shape by a finite simplicial complex with explicit face relations.
examples: A triangulated surface can be encoded by vertices, edges, and higher-dimensional faces together with incidence data
counterexamples: A cloud of points with no adjacency or face data is not yet a simplicial complex

rules.name: Persistent homology filtration seed
rules.input_form: filtered family of complexes or spaces
preconditions: A filtration parameter and compatible inclusions are fixed
rules.operation: Track topological features across a filtration instead of at one isolated scale.
examples: Changing scale in a point-cloud filtration reveals which connected components and cycles persist robustly
counterexamples: Reading topology from one isolated scale only loses persistence information

rules.name: Nerve reconstruction seed
rules.input_form: family of overlapping sets or local patches
preconditions: Overlap relations among sets are fixed
rules.operation: Build combinatorial topology from overlap data through the nerve construction.
examples: Sensor or sample coverage can be summarized by intersection patterns encoded in a nerve complex
counterexamples: Recording only set counts without overlap relations is insufficient for nerve-based topology

rules.name: Nearest-neighbor search seed
rules.input_form: finite metric or Euclidean sample set with query points
preconditions: A metric or geometric search space is fixed
rules.operation: Use geometric structure to prune search for nearest neighbors.
examples: Spatial indexing can prune large parts of a point set when exact or approximate neighbor queries are asked repeatedly
counterexamples: Treating all search problems as if metric structure offers no pruning opportunity is invalid

rules.name: Arrangement complexity seed
rules.input_form: finite family of geometric objects with incidences
preconditions: The active family of objects and incidence conventions are fixed
rules.operation: Analyze geometric arrangements through subdivisions, incidences, and event complexity.
examples: Line or segment arrangements are understood through cells, intersections, and boundary incidences rather than raw drawing alone
counterexamples: Counting only input objects without their induced subdivisions loses arrangement complexity

rules.name: Witness complex seed
rules.input_form: landmark set with witness relations from sampled data
preconditions: A landmark selection and witness rule are fixed
rules.operation: Compress sampled topology through landmark-based witness-complex construction.
examples: Large point clouds can be compressed topologically by landmark-based simplicial summaries rather than full dense complexes
counterexamples: Selecting landmarks with no witness rule does not automatically produce a witness complex

rules.name: Persistence stability seed
rules.input_form: filtered data set under controlled perturbation
preconditions: A filtration metric and perturbation model are fixed
rules.operation: Control persistence summaries under bounded perturbations of filtered data.
examples: Small changes in point-cloud data should not arbitrarily destroy every persistent feature when the filtration metric is well chosen
counterexamples: Expecting identical persistence summaries after arbitrary large perturbations is invalid

rules.name: Mapper summary seed
rules.input_form: data set with lens function, cover, and clustering rule
preconditions: A lens, cover, and local clustering procedure are fixed
rules.operation: Summarize high-dimensional data by a pullback-cover clustering graph.
examples: Coarse topological summaries can reveal branching or loop-like organization in structured data sets
counterexamples: Clustering data once with no cover or lens structure is not automatically a mapper construction

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion
rules.input_form: objects A and B with a valid composition law
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces
counterexamples: Composing incompatible objects is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
rules.input_form: object A with invertibility conditions
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity
counterexamples: Assuming inverses exist without conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Constraint propagation expansion
rules.input_form: state with constraints C and transform T
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Propagate constraints through each accepted transformation step.
examples: Positivity or boundedness constraints should be preserved or updated after transformation
counterexamples: Dropping constraints silently is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Boundary condition integration expansion
rules.input_form: model equation with boundary or endpoint constraints
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Include boundary and endpoint constraints in the active model state before solving.
examples: Differential models require boundary or initial data to identify admissible solution families
counterexamples: Solving while ignoring required boundary conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Conservation tracking expansion
rules.input_form: model evolution with candidate conserved quantity Q
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Track whether declared conserved quantities remain invariant under model evolution.
examples: Energy-like quantities can be validated as conserved under symmetry assumptions
counterexamples: Declaring conservation without validation is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion
rules.input_form: approximation method and tolerance epsilon
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Attach explicit error bounds or estimates to approximation-driven outputs.
examples: Numerical approximations should report residual or tolerance-constrained error
counterexamples: Reporting approximations without any error control is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Parameter sensitivity expansion
rules.input_form: model output O(theta) with parameter vector theta
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Quantify how parameter perturbations affect outputs and derived conclusions.
examples: Small parameter shifts can cause large output changes near bifurcation or instability regions
counterexamples: Assuming robustness with no sensitivity analysis is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Symmetry detection expansion
rules.input_form: equation or model M
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Detect and record symmetry transformations that preserve model structure.
examples: Translation or rotation symmetries can simplify derivations and reduce state dimensionality
counterexamples: Attributing symmetry to a model that breaks it under constraints is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Dimensionless reduction expansion
rules.input_form: dimensionful equation with characteristic scales
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rescale equations by characteristic magnitudes to expose dimensionless groups.
examples: Dimensionless groups often reveal dominant mechanisms and asymptotic regimes
counterexamples: Mixing inconsistent scales yields invalid normalization
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Solver branch admissibility expansion
rules.input_form: problem state and candidate branch family
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Choose solver branches by matching structural form, assumptions, and goal type.
examples: Optimization, proof, and simulation branches require different admissibility logic
counterexamples: Selecting branches on keywords alone is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Degenerate case handling expansion
rules.input_form: rule with potential degenerate parameter regimes
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Split and handle degenerate regimes explicitly instead of forcing generic formulas.
examples: Singular, zero, or limiting parameter cases often require separate derivation paths
counterexamples: Applying generic rules to singular cases without modification is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Proof obligation expansion
rules.input_form: candidate theorem-level claim
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Convert claims into explicit proof obligations before acceptance.
examples: Hypotheses, domain conditions, and intermediate lemmas should be listed explicitly
counterexamples: Accepting claims with missing obligations is invalid
